proposed_english: there is not / it is not (Lyc. negative existential)
rationale: Recurring on this page (lines 3, 4, 19, 22) as a negative-existential predicate. ⲕⲁⲟⲛ may be a Lycopolitan variant or corruption of ϣⲟⲟⲡ/ⲟⲩⲟⲛ in negative contexts. Functions as 'is not, there is none.' Distinguished from but parallel to standard ⲙⲛ̄/ⲙⲛ̄-ⲟⲩⲟⲛ.
Hapax on this page. Paired with ⲡⲕⲁⲣⲡⲟⲥ 'fruit' suggests 'tree' (possibly scribal variant of ⲡϣⲏⲛ or related to ⲧⲱϩⲙ 'mix' applied to a vegetative/agricultural register). Confidence low.
Line 9 noun paired with ⲡⲧⲭⲱⲍⲙⲉ 'the defilement.' Possibly Lyc. for ϩⲟϥ 'snake' or ϩⲁⲓⲃⲉⲥ 'shadow.' Flagged for parallels.
Lyc. ⲭⲱⲍⲙⲉ = Sah. ϫⲱϩⲙ̄ 'defile.' Substantive 'the defilement' fits cosmological context of corruption being purified.
Plural of ⲣⲡⲉ 'temple.' The Sixth Work concerns 'the temples of the upper place' being united and complete. Standard Coptic noun newly attested in this kephalaion.

proposed_english: this rich one / this rich man
rationale: Demonstrative ⲡⲓ- + ⲣⲙ̄ⲙⲁⲟ 'rich one' (already attested in vocabulary). Object of being 'heavy upon' — possibly a cosmic figure (the Father, an Aeon) or human ascetic burdened by the affliction described.
Privative ⲛⲁⲧ- + ⲣ̄-ⲍⲟ (where ⲍⲟ may be 'cease, fail' or 'fall') = 'without ceasing/falling' = unfailing, immovable. Modifies 'rest' (ⲙⲁⲧⲛⲉⲥ).
Greek loan φύω/φύσις used as Coptic verb — 'sprout, grow by nature.' Reflexive in 'they sprout themselves at the rivers' (Seventh Work).
ϣⲁⲙⲧ 'three' + Greek τύπος. Standard Manichaean-typological enumeration; the single Evil manifests in three types being purified.

proposed_english: the Tenth / Eleventh / Ninth / Eighth / Seventh / Sixth / Fifth / Fourth / Third / Second
rationale: Continuation of Lycopolitan feminine-ordinal series ⲧⲧⲙⲁⲍ-N (already attested partially in vocabulary): ⲙⲏⲧ 10, ⲙⲛ̄ⲧⲟⲩⲉ 11, ⲯⲓⲥ 9 (=ⲯⲓⲧ), ϣⲙⲟⲩⲛ 8, ⲥⲁⲱϥ 7 (=ⲥⲁϣϥ̄), ⲥⲁⲩ 6 (=ⲥⲟⲟⲩ), ϯⲟⲩ 5, ϥⲧⲁⲩ 4 (=ϥⲧⲟⲟⲩ), ⲥⲱⲁⲙⲧ 3 (=ϣⲟⲙⲧ̄), ⲥⲛⲉⲩ 2. Used to enumerate the cosmic/eschatological 'works' of the chapter.
